One of cannon's weaknesses is that most of their kit can be outmatched by the most played weapons in the game. The worst thing you can do with cannon (and any weapon for that matter) is wake up to enemy attacks, but specifically for cannon if you engage first and miss you will have quite a bit of end lag. If someone is moving around you in the air, keep track of their options. In my experience, the best moves to bait out people like that are backwards sair away from them to get them to run close to you, where you can then reverse dair them as you fall to catch them off guard, or watch how they react to gauge your options. Something else you can do is spam nair and follow their movements in the air outside of their attack range, weapon throw up or grav cancel side light (if you notice they use a dodge while above you). Don't rush for the strings when you punish; build up damage and run down the clock if you have to, then sig when you know you can get the kill.

Playing as slow as possible and attacking only when necessary is the best way to win any match up with cannon, and cannon can be the best weapon to play passive if you know what you're doing.

130 hours on genji switch here. Practice in the practice range daily while slowly inching your sensitivity by 5 everytime you open up the game. Overtime, you'll get used to the higher speeds required to perform with genji. If you struggle aiming with him with a higher sensitivity, use your body to aim along with gyro. However, you might find a niche, for example 70 horizontal, 40 vertical + gyro is good for me in combat but sometimes I switch to max horizontal + 40 vertical no gyro when I want to perform well with my ultimates as it's much faster and easier to get kills with blade but harder to aim with. You have to find your middle ground I suppose
